messages:
Ana (PM): Heads up — competitor surfaced a per-route SLA + deterministic fallback feature. Several customers are asking about predictable latency guarantees. Thoughts on urgency?

Matt (Eng Lead): Saw the writeup. Their model is routing by latency tier + cheap-model fallback. We have the pieces (routing + fallback) but not an exposed per-route SLA. Exposing it is product + infra work.

Ravi (Product Dir): Question: do we parity this (match their surface) or differentiate (bundle with cost-aware routing + quality guardrails)?

Sophie (Sales): Not theoretical — a few renewals hinge on "per-endpoint SLA". They want a contractual SLO for certain routes.

Diego (Design): From UX, a per-route SLA toggle is simple. Hard part is surfacing tradeoffs: cost, fallback behaviour, and rollback.

Nina (SE): On the implementation side: we can map existing model-priority + fallback weights to an MVP. The unknown is KV-cache continuity across fallback models. That could impact latency tail.

Ana (PM): Proposal: a two-phase plan. Phase A (parity MVP, 3w): expose per-route 99th-pct latency SLO flag + deterministic fallback to a lower-cost model. Phase B (differentiator, +4w): add cost-aware routing and per-route cost estimates. Launch criteria for MVP: 1) end-to-end telemetry for SLO, 2) fallback validated across 3 model families, 3) perf within 10% of targeted SLO on 90% of traffic profiles.

Matt (Eng Lead): 3 weeks for an MVP is aggressive. Spike + alpha in 3w is doable with 2 FTE engs + infra. KV cache semantics remain the biggest unknown and may push us.

Ravi (Product Dir): Tradeoffs spelled out: parity-first shortens sales cycle, differentiation increases product moat and upsell. We should prioritize parity to unblock renewals and schedule cost-aware routing immediately after.

Sophie (Sales): Agree — parity-first. Customers care about the guarantee now. Later, we can upsell a premium "cost guardrails" feature.

Diego (Design): UX plan: phase A = simple toggle + "estimate" modal that shows expected p99 and a rough cost delta. Phase B = interactive cost controls. I can sketch A by EOD.

Ana (PM): Decision: ship parity MVP first. I'll own the PRD and acceptance criteria. Matt, can you draft a short tech spec that lists engineers/time estimate and unknowns?

Matt (Eng Lead): Will do. I'll include KV-cache risk, rollout safety gates, and required infra metrics.

Nina (SE): I'll assemble the customer config matrix (token budgets, per-customer model variants, traffic shapes). Will attach examples from support tickets.

jira-bot: Created JD-1423: "Per-route SLA parity MVP (phase A)" and JD-1424: "Cost-aware routing (phase B)".

Ana (PM): Thanks — I'll update the roadmap, add the launch criteria to JD-1423, and schedule a 30min sync for scope alignment tomorrow. @Sophie please nominate the top 3 pilot customers. :thumbsup:

Sophie (Sales): On it. Names via DM.

Ravi (Product Dir): Big picture: this keeps us competitive quickly while buying time to build a stronger differentiator. Good call.

Matt (Eng Lead): +1. I'll put a tentative eng plan in JD-1423 and tag infra.

Diego (Design): I'll drop initial mocks in JD-1423 later today.

Ana (PM): Closing the thread — thanks everyone.
